questions.question_text: A business model is best described as the rationale of how an organisation:

options.A: Manages its supply chain logistics.
options.B: Creates, delivers, and captures value.
options.D: Only generates short-term profit.

questions.explanation: A business model describes the rationale for how an organisation creates, delivers, and captures value. The other options describe supporting activities, not the core definition.

questions.question_text: The Business Model Canvas is a strategic tool that visualises a company's model:

options.A: Through a single bar chart.
options.B: Only as a financial spreadsheet.
options.C: On a single page across nine interlinked building blocks (value proposition, infrastructure, customers, finances).
options.D: As a 50-page detailed report.

questions.explanation: The Business Model Canvas puts a company's model on a single page using nine interlinked building blocks covering the value proposition, infrastructure, customers, and finances.

questions.question_text: Which once-dominant Indian watchmaker eventually shut down after failing to adapt to changing technology and rising competition from brands like Titan?

options.A: HMT Watches
options.B: Voltas
options.D: Bajaj Electricals

questions.explanation: HMT Watches was once India's watch market leader. It shut down after failing to adapt to changing technology and to compete with Titan.

questions.question_text: Beyond logistics and inventory management, what valuable input do distributors typically feed back to manufacturers operating in distant markets?

options.A: Only invoice and billing data
options.B: Manufacturing blueprints
options.D: Ground-level market intelligence and customer feedback

questions.explanation: Distributors sit close to the market, so beyond logistics and inventory they feed ground-level market intelligence and customer feedback back to manufacturers.

questions.question_text: As the final link in a supply chain, what is the retailer's primary strategic function within the business ecosystem?

options.A: Managing wholesale-level inventory only
options.B: Serving as the direct interface with the end customer
options.D: Approving manufacturing designs

questions.explanation: As the final link in the supply chain, the retailer is the direct interface with the end customer. Wholesale inventory, logistics rates, and design approval sit upstream.

questions.question_text: Netflix, originally a DVD-by-mail service before pivoting to streaming, was founded by:

options.A: Jeff Bezos
options.B: Reed Hastings
options.D: Jack Dorsey

questions.explanation: Netflix was founded by Reed Hastings, who moved it from a DVD-by-mail rental service to a subscription streaming giant.

questions.question_text: The decline of MySpace in favour of Facebook is best explained by:

options.A: Facebook's acquisition of MySpace's servers
options.B: A drop in MySpace's content quality and rising spam, triggering negative network effects that pushed users toward Facebook's cleaner ecosystem
options.C: Facebook operating purely as a local classifieds board
options.D: MySpace introducing a costly subscription fee

questions.explanation: MySpace's content quality fell and spam rose, creating negative network effects. Users migrated to Facebook's cleaner ecosystem, so the decline came from a worse user experience.

questions.question_text: If an Uber dashboard shows riders in a zone waiting 20+ minutes for a match, which operational lever best restores marketplace liquidity?

options.A: Triggering surge pricing or push notifications to nearby drivers to rebalance supply
options.B: Temporarily banning new rider sign-ups
options.C: Charging riders a flat access fee to browse driver profiles
options.D: Disabling GPS tracking in that zone

questions.explanation: Long rider waits mean supply is short. Surge pricing or push notifications to nearby drivers rebalance supply and demand and restore liquidity. Banning sign-ups or disabling GPS does not fix it.

questions.question_text: Which platform launch strategy involves the operator first fulfilling transactions itself (e.g., through an owned fleet or in-house inventory) before opening the market to third-party participants?

options.A: Micro-market strategy
options.B: Follow-the-Rabbit strategy
options.D: Big-Bang seeding strategy

questions.explanation: In the Follow-the-Rabbit strategy, the operator first fulfils transactions itself (own fleet or inventory) to validate demand, then opens the market to third-party participants.

questions.question_text: An independent filmmaker wants to showcase a short film with high visual fidelity, advanced analytics, and no third-party ad interruptions. Which platform strategy fits best?

options.A: YouTube's fully automated, ad-supported recommendation engine
options.B: Craigslist's local classifieds video section
options.C: A generic blog's embedded video widget
options.D: Vimeo's ad-free, subscription-based model geared toward creative control

questions.explanation: Vimeo's ad-free, subscription-based model gives creators high visual fidelity, analytics, and creative control, with no third-party ad interruptions.

questions.question_text: Which metric would best capture the "liquidity" of a freelance marketplace such as Upwork?

options.A: The number of fonts used on the homepage
options.B: Total headcount at the company's headquarters
options.D: The percentage of posted jobs that result in a successful hire

questions.explanation: Marketplace liquidity is the ease with which supply and demand match. On Upwork, the share of posted jobs that end in a successful hire measures this directly.

questions.question_text: Which platform is frequently cited for using behavioural data to power "Personalised Recommendations" for music and audio content?

options.A: Zomato
options.B: Ola
options.D: eBay

questions.explanation: Spotify uses behavioural data (listening history) to power personalised recommendations for music and audio. Zomato, Ola, and eBay are not cited for this.

questions.question_text: How does data analytics on a marketplace like eBay specifically empower its "Sellers"?

options.A: By auto-generating legally binding contracts
options.B: By guaranteeing a sale regardless of listing quality
options.C: By surfacing market-trend and pricing-dynamics insights they can act on
options.D: By exposing every buyer's home address

questions.explanation: eBay's data analytics gives sellers insights into market trends and pricing dynamics they can act on. It cannot guarantee sales or expose buyers' private data.

questions.question_text: Why is "disintermediation" considered a structural risk for service marketplaces like Urban Company or Airbnb?

options.A: Because buyers and sellers may move transactions off-platform to avoid paying service fees
options.B: Because it requires excessive data storage
options.C: Because too many users overload the servers
options.D: Because it slows down internet speeds

questions.explanation: Disintermediation is a risk because buyers and sellers may take transactions off-platform to avoid service fees. This leaks the platform's revenue.

questions.question_text: A customer is anxious about receiving counterfeit cosmetics online. Which Nykaa value proposition would most directly reassure them?

options.A: Extensive product selection
options.B: Authenticity and direct sourcing from brands
options.D: In-house private labels

questions.explanation: Nykaa's value proposition of authenticity and direct sourcing from brands addresses fears of counterfeit cosmetics.

questions.question_text: Nykaa wants to deepen its "multi-sided" platform model. Which new participant group would be the most natural addition?

options.A: Auto-repair mechanics
options.B: Heavy-machinery manufacturers
options.D: A pure offline-only retail arm

questions.explanation: Nykaa's multi-sided model brings together brands, customers, and content creators. Beauty influencers and makeup experts are the most natural new participant group.

questions.question_text: An insurance provider wants to reach more customers without hiring additional agents. How should it apply the Policybazaar-style marketplace model?

options.A: Charge users a fee just to view policy details
options.B: Rely solely on physical mail campaigns
options.C: List its products on the marketplace to tap into the platform's existing user base
options.D: Shut down its own website entirely

questions.explanation: Listing its products on the marketplace lets the insurer tap the platform's existing user base without hiring more agents, as Policybazaar's model does.

questions.question_text: Which metric captures the total value of all transactions processed through a B2B marketplace, before deducting the platform's own commission?

options.A: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV)
options.B: Net Profit
options.D: Inventory Turnover Ratio

questions.explanation: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) is the total value of all transactions processed through a marketplace, before deducting the platform's commission.

questions.question_text: What primarily allowed Zoom to disrupt video-conferencing incumbents like Cisco WebEx and Microsoft Teams in its early growth phase?

options.A: It was the only completely free option on the market
options.B: It shipped pre-bundled with Windows
options.C: It relied exclusively on on-premise servers
options.D: Its simplicity and reliable audio/video quality even on weak connections

questions.explanation: Zoom disrupted WebEx and Teams through its simplicity and reliable audio/video quality even on weak connections.

questions.question_text: A SaaS company bills a customer strictly according to the number of API calls consumed each month. This pricing model is known as:

options.A: Tiered pricing
options.B: Perpetual licensing
options.D: Usage-based pricing

questions.explanation: Charging strictly by consumption, such as the number of API calls, is usage-based (pay-as-you-go) pricing.

questions.question_text: A customer downgrades from the "Pro" plan to "Basic", reducing the monthly revenue they contribute. This is best described as:

options.A: Churn
options.B: Contraction
options.D: Acquisition

questions.explanation: A customer moving from a higher plan to a lower one stays a customer but pays less. This is contraction, whereas churn is a full cancellation.

questions.question_text: You're selling SaaS to a 50,000-employee enterprise. Best-practice guidance suggests your sales motion should be:

options.A: Identical to a self-serve small-business sale
options.B: Tailored specifically to enterprise buying processes and stakeholders
options.D: Fully automated through chatbots only

questions.explanation: Enterprise buyers have complex buying processes and many stakeholders. The sales motion must be tailored to them, not a self-serve approach.

questions.question_text: Users adopt a product because it's genuinely useful and organically invite colleagues, with no salesperson involved in the process. This growth motion is known as:

options.A: Enterprise Field Sales
options.B: Sales-Led Growth
options.D: Product-Led Growth (PLG)

questions.explanation: When users adopt a product because it is useful and organically invite colleagues, with no salesperson involved, the growth motion is Product-Led Growth (PLG).

questions.question_text: Which Indian FinTech company is commonly cited as a leading example offering mobile wallets, UPI payments, and utility bill payments?

options.A: ZestMoney
options.B: Paytm
options.D: Adobe

questions.explanation: Paytm is the Indian FinTech example known for mobile wallets, UPI payments, and utility bill payments.

questions.question_text: Which concept best explains the fundamental reason a customer chooses a SaaS product over legacy on-premise software?

options.A: Revenue generation
options.B: Value proposition
options.D: Churn rate

questions.explanation: The value proposition is the fundamental reason a customer chooses a SaaS product over legacy on-premise software. Revenue, CAPEX, and churn are business-side measures.

questions.question_text: Offering existing users a $50 credit for successfully referring a friend to sign up is an example of:

options.A: A customer referral program
options.B: Content marketing
options.D: Vertical SaaS

questions.explanation: Giving existing users a credit for referring a friend who signs up is a customer referral program.

questions.question_text: You have an idea for a new app but build only its essential core feature first to test market interest before investing further. This stripped-down version is called the:

options.A: Product roadmap
options.B: Final product
options.D: Minimum Viable Product (MVP)

questions.explanation: Building only the essential core feature to test market interest before investing further is a Minimum Viable Product (MVP).

questions.question_text: What is the defining characteristic of a "Neobank"?

options.A: It operates the largest network of physical branches
options.B: It operates entirely through digital channels with no physical branch network
options.D: It deals exclusively in physical gold

questions.explanation: A Neobank is a digital-only bank. It operates entirely through digital channels with no physical branch network.

questions.question_text: Why is Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) an especially critical metric for WealthTech platforms compared to traditional banks?

options.A: Because customers switch banks daily
options.B: Because WealthTech firms generate no revenue at all
options.C: Because regulators fix the CAC by law
options.D: Because per-transaction margins are thin, so users must be acquired cost-efficiently to remain profitable

questions.explanation: WealthTech platforms earn thin per-transaction margins, so users must be acquired cost-efficiently. This makes CAC especially critical compared with traditional banks.

questions.question_text: Practo's "Surgery Discovery" vertical lets patients book high-value surgeries end-to-end through the platform. How does Practo primarily monetise this service?

options.A: Selling surgical instruments directly to hospitals
options.B: A flat monthly membership fee charged to patients
options.C: Billing doctors for the electricity used during the procedure
options.D: A commission taken on the surgery revenue

questions.explanation: Practo's Surgery Discovery vertical earns revenue as a commission on the surgery bookings made through the platform.

questions.question_text: Which factor is most often cited as part of the "robust supporting ecosystem" that has enabled D2C brands to flourish in India?

options.A: The elimination of all last-mile delivery services
options.B: Horizontal platforms like Amazon, social media, and digital payment systems
options.C: A full return to offline-only village retail
options.D: A nationwide ban on product R&D

questions.explanation: Horizontal platforms such as Amazon, social media, and digital payment systems form the robust supporting ecosystem that lets D2C brands sell directly online.

questions.question_text: Why has boAt been able to price its audio products more competitively than legacy premium audio brands?

options.A: Lower corporate overheads and reduced spend on mass-media brand advertising
options.B: Because it conducts no R&D whatsoever
options.C: Because it sells through a single flagship store only
options.D: Because its products are made from low-cost cardboard casing

questions.explanation: boAt kept corporate overheads low and spent little on mass-media advertising, which let it price below legacy premium audio brands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best captures Mamaearth's core value proposition as a D2C brand?

options.A: Offering the cheapest possible chemical-heavy formulations
options.B: Selling exclusively through premium physical boutiques
options.D: Safe, toxin-free alternatives for baby and personal care

questions.explanation: Mamaearth's core D2C value proposition is safe, toxin-free alternatives for baby and personal care.

questions.question_text: How does boAt's product design philosophy differ from that of traditional premium audio brands?

options.A: boAt products are made entirely of wood
options.B: There is no meaningful design difference - only price differs
options.C: boAt products are sold in only one colour
options.D: Traditional designs were bulky and utilitarian, while boAt emphasises youth-centric, fashion-forward aesthetics

questions.explanation: Traditional audio designs were bulky and utilitarian, whereas boAt emphasises youth-centric, fashion-forward aesthetics.

questions.question_text: Why is influencer marketing particularly effective for a youth-focused D2C brand like boAt?

options.A: Because young audiences follow influencers, and seeing them use trendy products builds social proof and desirability
options.B: Because influencers work without any compensation
options.C: Because influencers personally manufacture the products
options.D: Because it is the only route into physical retail stores

questions.explanation: Young audiences follow influencers. Seeing them use trendy products builds social proof and desirability for a youth-focused D2C brand like boAt.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between a "vanity metric" and an "actionable metric"?

options.A: Actionable metrics are always numerically larger
options.B: Vanity metrics are free to track; actionable metrics cost money
options.C: Vanity metrics look impressive but offer little strategic insight, while actionable metrics directly inform business decisions
options.D: Vanity metrics are used only by technology companies

questions.explanation: Vanity metrics look impressive but give little strategic insight. Actionable metrics directly inform business decisions.

questions.question_text: What was a major impact of Web 2.0 on the creator economy?

options.A: A sharp decline in overall internet usage
options.B: The growth of user-generated content and interactive platforms
options.C: A steep decline in social media adoption
options.D: The disappearance of blogging as a format

questions.explanation: Web 2.0 enabled user-generated content and interactive platforms, which fuelled the growth of the creator economy.

questions.question_text: How does consistent KPI tracking support "informed decision-making" within an organisation?

options.A: It guarantees the CEO's judgment is always correct
options.B: It removes the need for management meetings entirely
options.C: It lets leaders base decisions on quantifiable data instead of gut instinct
options.D: It automatically makes strategic decisions on the manager's behalf

questions.explanation: Consistent KPI tracking lets leaders base decisions on quantifiable data instead of gut instinct.

questions.question_text: The Balanced Scorecard evaluates an organisation from which four perspectives?

options.A: Financial, Customer, Internal Process, Learning & Growth
options.B: Marketing, Sales, HR, Operations
options.D: Short-term, Long-term, Daily, Monthly

questions.explanation: The Balanced Scorecard views an organisation from four perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Process, and Learning & Growth.

questions.question_text: Which metric in a manufacturing business model most directly measures operational efficiency?

options.A: Churn rate
options.B: Machine utilisation rate
options.D: Average daily rate

questions.explanation: Machine utilisation rate measures how much of a machine's capacity is used. It directly reflects operational efficiency in manufacturing.

questions.question_text: Historically, creators depended on intermediaries such as publishers or record labels. What has fundamentally changed in today's creator economy?

options.A: Increased reliance on intermediaries
options.B: Direct creator-to-audience connection enabled by digital platforms
options.D: The elimination of all monetisation options

questions.explanation: Digital platforms let creators connect directly with their audience, reducing dependence on publishers and record labels.

questions.question_text: Why is "creator retention" a critical metric for creator-economy platforms?

options.A: Because end-users on the platform don't matter
options.B: Because higher creator earnings and better tools reduce creator churn, sustaining the content supply
options.C: Because creators typically stay regardless of how much they earn
options.D: Because retention has no relationship to monetisation

questions.explanation: Higher creator earnings and better tools reduce creator churn. This sustains the content supply, which is why creator retention is critical.

questions.question_text: In an on-demand or subscription business, what is generally considered the "golden rule" target for the LTV:CAC ratio?
questions.explanation: The golden-rule target for LTV:CAC in on-demand and subscription businesses is 3:1. Customer lifetime value should be about three times the cost of acquiring the customer.

questions.question_text: Why are NFTs considered useful for digital art, even though the underlying image files can be copied?

options.A: They convert digital art into a physical product
options.B: They make copying technically impossible
options.C: They automatically delete all duplicate image files
options.D: They provide verifiable proof of ownership and authenticity despite the existence of copies

questions.explanation: An NFT gives verifiable proof of ownership and authenticity for a digital asset, even though copies of the image file can exist.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a defining feature of cryptocurrency systems?

options.A: Centralised control by a single bank
options.B: Fixed exchange rates set by national governments
options.D: Decentralisation enabled by blockchain technology

questions.explanation: Cryptocurrency systems are decentralised, enabled by blockchain technology, with no single bank in control.

questions.question_text: A restaurant currently pays 27% commission to a food-delivery duopoly. If it integrates with ONDC, what is the most direct way this improves its profitability?

options.A: It should raise menu prices to absorb the 27% fee
options.B: It can save a substantial portion of the commission by routing orders through ONDC, improving its net margin
options.C: It should sell only its own branded merchandise and ignore delivery entirely
options.D: It should stop offering delivery altogether

questions.explanation: By routing orders through ONDC, the restaurant can save a substantial part of the 27% commission and improve its net margin.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the protocol layer connecting buyer apps and seller apps within ONDC?

options.A: To let any buyer app transact with any seller app, regardless of which company built each one
options.B: To operate as a single monopoly platform
options.C: To set fixed prices for all goods sold on the network
options.D: To hold customer funds like a bank

questions.explanation: The ONDC protocol layer lets any buyer app transact with any seller app, irrespective of which company built each one.

questions.question_text: An online store recorded 20,000 visitors and 400 completed purchases in a month. What is its conversion rate?
questions.explanation:
Conversion rate = purchases / visitors x 100.

Step 1: 400 / 20,000 = 0.02.

Step 2: 0.02 x 100 = 2%.

questions.question_text: Can a neighbourhood Kirana store function as a "Seller Side App" on ONDC?

options.A: Yes, but only if it exclusively sells electronics
options.B: Yes - if it chooses to, it can list itself directly on ONDC as a seller-side application
options.C: No, it must always sell through Amazon or Flipkart
options.D: No, only large national brands are permitted to be apps

questions.explanation: ONDC is an open network, so a Kirana store can list itself directly as a seller-side application if it chooses to.

questions.question_text: The challenge a new two-sided marketplace faces in attracting both buyers and sellers simultaneously - since neither side wants to join first without the other already present - is commonly known as:

options.A: The chicken-and-egg problem
options.B: The churn spiral
options.D: The vanity metric problem

questions.explanation: The chicken-and-egg problem is the challenge of attracting buyers and sellers at the same time, since neither wants to join first.
